climate_pressure: Projected rainfall/drought pressures exacerbating already stressed water resources.
documented_impact: Possible further reductions in water/livelihood security and greater service/resource competition.
fcv_mediator: Pre-existing grievances, unequal/strained service access, resource-management failures and contested allocation can shape how scarcity is experienced.
possible_consequence: The 2023 roadmap warns of disputes, social discontent and anti-refugee sentiment; no measured climate-attributable violence or local incident trend.
alternative_explanations: Over-extraction, infrastructure, resource governance, poverty, service investment and regional politics independently affect water stress and social relations.
uncertainty: Conditional 2023 synthesis, not a causal evaluation. Not projected onto the small Mafraq survey or used to stigmatize refugees; climate is neither the sole cause of scarcity nor proof of violence.
resilience_factors: The roadmap recommends integrated climate-security institutions, while local coping and water-system maintenance evidence identify capacities; proven conflict reduction is not asserted.
compact_statement: Jordan's 2023 roadmap warns that climate-exacerbated water/livelihood pressures can interact with pre-existing grievances and strained allocation to weaken cohesion; this is a conditional national mechanism, not a measured local climate–violence effect.
